newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open higher Tuesday, with the complex seen consolidating after losses in the past few days.

Today, German Finance Minister Waigel and Bundesbank President Tietmeyer were reported to be near an agreement on the dispute over revaluating Bundesbank gold reserves to help Germany meet European Monetary Union (EMU) criteria.
COMEX August gold, now the active contract, was called unchanged to $0.20 firmer from Monday's close of $346.50 an ounce.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $344.10/60 against the London morning fix of $343.80 and Monday's New York close of $343.30/70.
COMEX gold stocks rose 10,031 ounces Monday to 878,200 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks were up 1,249,245 ounces at 201,446,110 ounces.
COMEX July silver was called up 0.5 to 1.00 cent from Monday's finish of $4.698.
NYMEX July platinum was called up $1.00 to $2.00 from the previous close of $398.70, with NYMEX September palladium called the same from yesterday's close of $164.30.

In the bullion market, palladium lending rates jumped again overnight to around 50 percent for the one month forward from around 30 percent Monday as the physical market continues to suffer from the absence of Russian exports in the past five months.
